correctness.rationale: There are exactly 96 balanced four-mers and 52 reverse-complement orbits, including 8 singletons. Orbit selection is logically equivalent to closure; every comma violation and distance violation has a forbidden support of size at most 3. The finite exact search branches exhaustively and prunes only with rigorously justified greedy incompatibility-class upper bounds. It establishes strict maxima 21/17/7 and enumerates 136/16/72 equality codebooks. Every output codebook is subsequently direct-checked against the original definitions; all class counts and fixed-word values are reconstructed. Python stdlib verifier and exact result inventory have been executed together, yielding VERIFY_OK. No infinite-length claim or unverified computational extrapolation is made.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Upper bounds on an unrestricted code family may give weaker ceilings but do not establish an exact restricted optimum or its optimizer counts. A general GC-only upper bound also does not make the RC-closure and comma-free constraints automatic. Reverse-complement separation requires d_H(x,RC(y)) positive for all selected x,y; if C is closed and nonempty, choosing y=RC(x) makes this distance zero, so the separation family cannot contain these closed codebooks at positive separation.

evidence: Forbidding every proper prefix/suffix match (non-overlapping) is stronger than merely forbidding every misframed codeword splice (comma-free); the explicit 21-word example verifies its feasible size under the latter grammar.
Binary length-six comma-free distance-two code classifications concern a different alphabet and word length; the claimed 96-word balanced universe is quaternary at length four.

Single-deletion correction forbids shared deletion descendants, whereas the present condition forbids only cross-boundary splices and close framed Hamming pairs; neither type of channel constraint automatically entails the other.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A general non-overlapping code is comma-free, but the converse need not hold: a bound for non-overlapping codes cannot imply a bound for the larger comma-free class. Equal numerical 17 at one threshold does not imply matching concepts or maximizers (the present distance-two optimum has 16 labeled codebooks, each with one RC-fixed word). Six-bit binary comma-free and four-letter deletion-code theorems have no evident reductions that force all three present maxima or equality counts. Direct earlier-record comparisons used only recoverable claim summaries, without reconsidering historical scientific status.

originality.rationale: The exact joint statement (quaternary four-letter GC-two comma-freeness, reverse-complement closure, Hamming-distance thresholds and complete optimum census) is not implied by the inspected primary bounds for unrestricted comma-free codes nor by constant-GC DNA codes with reverse-complement separation. Direct semantic comparison of actual constraints, rather than title similarity, distinguishes previous exact non-overlapping, binary and deletion-code results. Multiple targeted public-literature and published-finding corpus record searches found no corresponding sharp three-threshold classification. This is a qualified best-knowledge originality assessment, not a proof of global historical priority.
residual_risks: Unindexed older literature or unpublished exact enumerations may have an equivalent classification; the searches do not certify historical priority.

The broader literature of biological circular codes sometimes studies overlapping word sets with alternate synchronization definitions; no implication from such a formulation has been established here.
No independent external audit of the executable exhaustive proof has been performed.

value.rationale: Four-nucleotide DNA barcodes provide a compact, natural test case for jointly imposing exact half-GC content, strand reversal symmetry and frame synchronization, with distinct framed substitution-detection and substitution-correction requirements. The sharp 21→17→7 cardinality tradeoff gives exact constrained coding capacity at three canonical Hamming thresholds, while the complete 224-optimum census and symmetry/fixed-point classification provide structural design information for codebook selection. This is not a routine special case of a known unconstrained code bound: intersecting comma-freeness, RC closure and GC content changes feasibility in ways not captured by separate constraint counts.
